facts.text: Santa Monica was named after Santa Monica, California, by Clarence Ayers, president of the American Life Insurance Company, who funded its development in 1925.
The community sits at the end of a former Missouri Pacific spur, located on Farm Roads 1018 and 1420, fourteen miles southeast of Raymondville in southeastern Willacy County.
The town’s coordinates are 26°21′56″N 97°35′24″W, placing it just south of the Gulf Coast.
Some ranches surrounding Santa Monica date back to the early 1800s, reflecting the area’s long agricultural heritage.
The 2020 census recorded 33 housing units in Santa Monica, with an average density of 93.5 per square mile.
The Texas State Historical Association preserves Santa Monica’s history through its Handbook of Texas Online entry, which was last revised in 1995.
